answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting work, whether sourcing pigment, surveying a meadow, or calculating a star’s zenith angle. A smart contract holds each bond separately, so one deposit cannot back multiple identities. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month: generating names is cheap, but turning them into active sellers carries a capital cost that scales with the attack.
